title: Converting Volume Units
subtitle: Moving between mL, L, cm³ and m³ without losing a zero.
objectives: Explain why the cubic jump is 1,000 and not 100

cards.title: The jumps are bigger than you expect
cards.text: Going from cm to m is 100. Going from cm³ to m³ is a million. Cubes punish you three times over.

cards.title: Millilitres and litres: 1,000
cards.text: This one is small and friendly. Learn it cold.
points: **1 L = 1,000 mL.** Multiply to go down, divide to go up.
**Three decimal places**, every time.

question.text: Convert 3.2 litres to millilitres. Digits only.

cards.title: Why cm³ to m³ is a million
cards.text: A metre is 100 cm. A cubic metre is 100 cm in all three directions.
points: **The 100 gets cubed**, because volume has three dimensions.
**This is where people lose zeros.** Expect the big number.

cards.title: Why three dimensions multiply
cards.text: Press each edge length. The volume grows by the cube of the edge, not by the edge.

question.text: 1 cubic metre equals how many cubic centimetres?

cards.title: Same trap in area, half as bad
cards.text: Squares get the jump twice; cubes get it three times.
points: **1 m² = 10,000 cm²**: the 100 squared.
**Count the dimensions** and you know the jump.

cards.title: Did the number move the right way?
cards.text: A bigger unit should give a smaller number. If it got bigger, you went backwards.
points: **cm³ to m³**: the number must get smaller.
**L to mL**: the number must get bigger.
**Ask which unit is bigger** before you calculate.
**A sanity check costs two seconds.**

cards.title: Ten times bigger, a thousand times more
cards.alt: A tiny cube beside a hollow cube ten times larger in every direction, with a layer of the tiny cubes on its floor
cards.text: Ten along, ten across, ten up. That is where the 1,000 comes from.

cards.title: Capacitors are measured in millionths
cards.text: The fan capacitor says 2.5 µF. That µ is micro. One millionth of a farad.
points: **A farad is enormous**, so real parts are measured in micro.
**2.5 µF** is 0.0000025 F written sensibly.
**Same trick as powers of ten**: move the size into the prefix.
**Mix up µF and nF** and the motor will not start.

question.text: Convert 2,000,000 cm³ to cubic metres. Digits only.

cards.title: Engine size is a volume, written three ways
cards.text: A 2.0 litre engine, a 2000 cc engine and a 2000 cm³ engine are all the same engine.
points: **cc means cubic centimetre.** It is the same unit.
**It is the volume the pistons sweep**, not the size of the car.
**Three names, one number.** The conversion is the point.

terms.def: Rewrite a measurement in a different unit, same amount.
Cubic centimetre; the same as cm³ and as mL.
A length factor raised to the power of three.

cards.title: What to remember
points: 1 L = 1,000 mL. Learn it cold.
1 m³ = 1,000,000 cm³, because 100 gets cubed.
Bigger unit, smaller number. Check before you move on.
cc, cm³ and mL are three names for one unit.

teacher.summary: Term 2 Week 7 Math, the first of the scope's two conversion weeks. The lesson is organised around the one thing that actually goes wrong (the cubic jump) and makes it a consequence of dimensions rather than a number to memorise: 100 cubed, once per direction. Area is shown beside it so the pattern generalises. The engine card is doing real work: cc, cm³ and mL are three names he already half-knows for one unit, and connecting them removes a whole category of confusion.
discussion: Why is the cubic jump a million?
Which unit is bigger, and so which way should the number move?
Why is an engine measured in volume at all?
extension: Check the cc rating on any motorbike or car and convert it to litres.
Measure a box in cm, find its volume, then write it in m³.
misconceptions: That cm³ to m³ is a factor of 100.
That cc is a different unit from cm³.
Moving the decimal the wrong way.
